pathway.title: Caesars Entertainment, Inc. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: 1. The lease obligations are larger than the debt. Long-term financing obligations of 13,157 exceed total debt of 11,807 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Mechanism: the leases are fixed, rise with inflation, and their cost sits in interest expense, outside Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: lease-adjusted leverage of 5.30x to 6.95x (CP-1 C4, C5), not the debt-only 3.29x, sets leverage tolerance. Analyst Interpretation. 2. A change of control is pending with unknown financing. The Merger Agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at 31 US dollars per share in cash, subject to stockholder, antitrust and gaming approvals, with an end date that can extend to November 27, 2027 (CP-1A transaction summary). Mechanism: a private owner may add acquisition debt and change the capital structure; the issuer itself lists "increased leverage from the proposed transaction" as a risk (CP-1A Documentary Fact row). Implication: the current credit view may not hold after closing; monitoring posture is event-driven. Documentary Fact for the terms; Insufficient Information for the financing. 3. Coverage is thin on the full basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, including lease interest, 1.57x over the last twelve months; after cash rent it covers cash interest on debt 2.87x (CP-1 C6). Mechanism: a fall in Adjusted EBITDA passes almost entirely to coverage because rent and interest are fixed. Implication: limited room for an earnings decline before debt service is strained. Analyst Interpretation. 4. Earnings are flat to slightly down. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,592 is below the FY2025 figure of 3,624, and the margin fell from 31.6% to 30.8% (CP-1 C1, C7); Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below Q2 2025. Las Vegas declined while Regional grew (CP-1A segment rows). Mechanism: Las Vegas is the largest Adjusted EBITDA segment, so its decline weighs on group cash flow. Implication: deleveraging from earnings growth is not in evidence. Documentary Fact via CP-1 and CP-1A. 5. Liquidity and maturities are not a near-term constraint. Liquidity of 2,928 at June 30, 2026 compares with estimated remaining 2026 debt service of about 425 and lease payments of about 687 (CP-1 liquidity). The first large maturities are the revolver and Term Loan A in 2028 (CP-1 maturity row). Implication: low near-term default risk from liquidity, assuming the capital structure is unchanged. Documentary Fact via CP-1. 6. Debt has been reduced modestly. Total debt face value fell from 11,905 to 11,807, after the 2027 notes were redeemed in July 2025 and share repurchases stopped in 2026 (CP-1, CP-1A governance rows). Implication: the trend is supportive but small relative to the lease-adjusted burden. Documentary Fact.

Documentary Fact. - Cash generation: LTM operating cash flow of 1,297 and free cash flow of 610 after capex (CP-1 C1, C2). Free cash flow is positive and rising as capex falls. blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The central transaction is a pending take-private. On May 27, 2026, Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and its merger subsidiary signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which "Merger Sub will merge with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation and direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming" (10-Q line 273). The release says the agreement was "announced on May 28, 2026" (release line 106). Each share converts into cash of "$31.00", plus a ticking fee if closing has not occurred by "June 26, 2027" (10-Q line 277). Documentary Fact.

Conditions and protection. Closing needs approval "by the holders of at least a majority of all of the outstanding shares", expiry of the HSR Act waiting period and "certain gaming regulatory approvals" (10-Q line 294). Either party may terminate if the merger has not closed by May 27, 2027, with automatic extensions to August 27, 2027 and November 27, 2027 while only regulatory conditions remain (10-Q line 296). Caesars would owe "a termination fee of $200 million" in specified circumstances; Fertitta Gaming would owe "a reverse termination fee of $450 million" if the merger fails on antitrust or gaming-law grounds or at the end date with only regulatory conditions open (10-Q lines 297 to 298). A no-shop applies from "July 11, 2026" (10-Q line 290). Documentary Fact.

Financing and existing debt. The supplied documents do not describe how Fertitta Gaming will fund the merger or how the existing CEI credit facilities, notes and VICI and GLPI leases are treated at closing. The 10-Q lists among its risks "the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all" and "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q line 1391). The Merger Agreement is exhibit 2.1 to the 8-K of May 28, 2026 (10-Q line 305), which is not in the source set. Insufficient Information.

Recent debt activity. On July 8, 2025, Caesars "fully redeemed all of the $546 million outstanding principal amount of the CEI Senior Notes due 2027", funded by revolver borrowings and proceeds of a note receivable from the WSOP trademark sale (10-K line 1367). No new bond issue is described for 2026 in the supplied documents; the six-month cash flows show revolver and term-loan borrowings and repayments (CP-1 cash-flow table). Earlier divestitures raised cash: the WSOP trademark for "$500 million" on October 29, 2024, and The LINQ Promenade for "$275 million" on December 12, 2024 (10-K lines 1053 to 1054). Documentary Fact.

Liquidity effect, as Analyst Interpretation: before closing, liquidity of about 2.9 billion (CP-1) covers the remaining 2026 debt service and lease payments the issuer estimates. After closing, liquidity and leverage depend on the acquisition financing, which is Not supplied.

fields.value: The central transaction is a pending take-private. On May 27, 2026, Caesars, Fertitta Gaming Holdco, LLC and its merger subsidiary signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger under which "Merger Sub will merge with and into the Company, with the Company continuing as the surviving corporation and direct wholly owned subsidiary of Fertitta Gaming" (10-Q line 273). The release says the agreement was "announced on May 28, 2026" (release line 106). Each share converts into cash of "$31.00", plus a ticking fee if closing has not occurred by "June 26, 2027" (10-Q line 277). Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Conditions and protection. Closing needs approval "by the holders of at least a majority of all of the outstanding shares", expiry of the HSR Act waiting period and "certain gaming regulatory approvals" (10-Q line 294). Either party may terminate if the merger has not closed by May 27, 2027, with automatic extensions to August 27, 2027 and November 27, 2027 while only regulatory conditions remain (10-Q line 296). Caesars would owe "a termination fee of $200 million" in specified circumstances; Fertitta Gaming would owe "a reverse termination fee of $450 million" if the merger fails on antitrust or gaming-law grounds or at the end date with only regulatory conditions open (10-Q lines 297 to 298). A no-shop applies from "July 11, 2026" (10-Q line 290). Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing and existing debt. The supplied documents do not describe how Fertitta Gaming will fund the merger or how the existing CEI credit facilities, notes and VICI and GLPI leases are treated at closing. The 10-Q lists among its risks "the risk that the financing required to fund the proposed transaction is not obtained on the terms anticipated or at all" and "risks associated with increased leverage from the proposed transaction" (10-Q line 1391). The Merger Agreement is exhibit 2.1 to the 8-K of May 28, 2026 (10-Q line 305), which is not in the source set. Insufficient Information.

On July 8, 2025, Caesars "fully redeemed all of the $546 million outstanding principal amount of the CEI Senior Notes due 2027", funded by revolver borrowings and proceeds of a note receivable from the WSOP trademark sale (10-K line 1367). No new bond issue is described for 2026 in the supplied documents; the six-month cash flows show revolver and term-loan borrowings and repayments (CP-1 cash-flow table). Earlier divestitures raised cash: the WSOP trademark for "$500 million" on October 29, 2024, and The LINQ Promenade for "$275 million" on December 12, 2024 (10-K lines 1053 to 1054). Documentary Fact.

fields.value: Caesars is a large, diversified gaming operator whose credit profile is set by heavy fixed obligations: about 11.8 billion of debt and about 13.2 billion of lease financing obligations to VICI and GLPI (CP-1 debt and lease rows). Debt-only leverage of 3.29x (CP-1 C3) understates the burden; with the leases, leverage is 6.95x on carrying amounts (CP-1 C4) or 5.30x on debt over Adjusted EBITDA after cash rent (CP-1 C5), and Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest only 1.57x (CP-1 C6). fields.value: Thesis: Caesars can service its current debt and leases from operations with adequate liquidity, but its lease-adjusted leverage is high, earnings are flat, and a pending change of control with unknown financing is the main credit risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 1. The lease obligations are larger than the debt. Long-term financing obligations of 13,157 exceed total debt of 11,807 at June 30, 2026 (CP-1). Mechanism: the leases are fixed, rise with inflation, and their cost sits in interest expense, outside Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: lease-adjusted leverage of 5.30x to 6.95x (CP-1 C4, C5), not the debt-only 3.29x, sets leverage tolerance. Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. A change of control is pending with unknown financing. The Merger Agreement was signed on May 27, 2026 at 31 US dollars per share in cash, subject to stockholder, antitrust and gaming approvals, with an end date that can extend to November 27, 2027 (CP-1A transaction summary). Mechanism: a private owner may add acquisition debt and change the capital structure; the issuer itself lists "increased leverage from the proposed transaction" as a risk (CP-1A Documentary Fact row). Implication: the current credit view may not hold after closing; monitoring posture is event-driven. Documentary Fact for the terms; Insufficient Information for the financing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Coverage is thin on the full basis. Adjusted EBITDA covers total net interest, including lease interest, 1.57x over the last twelve months; after cash rent it covers cash interest on debt 2.87x (CP-1 C6). Mechanism: a fall in Adjusted EBITDA passes almost entirely to coverage because rent and interest are fixed. Implication: limited room for an earnings decline before debt service is strained. Analyst Interpretation.

fields.value: 4. Earnings are flat to slightly down. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 3,592 is below the FY2025 figure of 3,624, and the margin fell from 31.6% to 30.8% (CP-1 C1, C7); Q2 2026 Adjusted EBITDA was below Q2 2025. Las Vegas declined while Regional grew (CP-1A segment rows). Mechanism: Las Vegas is the largest Adjusted EBITDA segment, so its decline weighs on group cash flow. Implication: deleveraging from earnings growth is not in evidence. Documentary Fact via CP-1 and CP-1A.

fields.value: 5. Liquidity and maturities are not a near-term constraint. Liquidity of 2,928 at June 30, 2026 compares with estimated remaining 2026 debt service of about 425 and lease payments of about 687 (CP-1 liquidity). The first large maturities are the revolver and Term Loan A in 2028 (CP-1 maturity row). Implication: low near-term default risk from liquidity, assuming the capital structure is unchanged. Implication: the trend is supportive but small relative to the lease-adjusted burden. Documentary Fact.
